problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=36.$ What is the second component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(t,y)=⟨\text{_____},y,\,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}=16.$ What is the first component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the ellipse 

$$
{x}^{2}+4{z}^{2}=16\,⟹\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}=1
$$

in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,z⟩=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t\in [0,2\pi ),
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =\frac{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}{4} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,y) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in [0,2\pi )$ and $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $4\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$
